mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate over the past month indicates monetary tightening, which increases discount rates for equity valuation, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals economic weakness and potential earnings deterioration, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) indicates broad demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative returns: SPX returns are positive in > 60% of such instances, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 3.0% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY), a further increase in the federal funds rate compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances during monetary tightening cycles when FEDFUNDS rises, or the regime-specific Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90.0 signals a manufacturing slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 90.0, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1.0% signals weak consumer demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST declines by more than 1.0%, or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, supporting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS rises, or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5% signals accelerating inflation, triggering a sell-off in equities and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises above 0.5%, or the Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
